tasks.prompt: Order an advanced coagulation control program using streaming current and settled quality feedback.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Class 3 plant in Alberta on a variable prairie river source using enhanced process control under provincial drinking water requirements in general terms.
tasks.configuration: Scope: control goal definition through a sustained closed loop coagulation program.

cards.label: Set settled turbidity, colour, and organics targets and the coagulant dose limits for the control program
Install and verify raw turbidity, pH, temperature, and streaming current signals against bench readings
Run jar tests across the raw water range to map dose response and set the feed forward dose table
Start feedback trimming in manual review mode so operators approve each suggested dose change
Compare suggested and actual settled quality daily for two weeks and tune the trim limits
Place the program in automatic trim within the approved limits and file the control strategy

tasks.explanation: Feed forward dosing from raw signals handles most of the change, feedback trim corrects the remainder, and automatic control is earned only after suggested doses are proven against settled quality.

tasks.prompt: Order a plant wide process control audit for a large conventional plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional senior operator team in Saskatchewan auditing control loops across a regional conventional plant.
tasks.configuration: Scope: audit planning through prioritized control improvements implemented.

cards.label: List every control loop from raw intake to clearwell and note its sensor, controller, and final element
Trend each loop for a representative month and mark loops that oscillate, saturate, or run in manual
Field verify the worst loops by comparing sensor readings with calibrated bench and portable instruments
Rank defects by treated water quality risk and by how often operators must intervene
Correct the highest risk defects first and retune each loop under normal production
Record the audit, the corrections, and the next audit date in the process control program file

tasks.explanation: An audit trends performance before touching hardware, ranks by quality risk, and retunes under production so improvements are proven rather than assumed.

tasks.prompt: Order an enhanced coagulation optimization study for disinfection byproduct control.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in Manitoba increasing organics removal to control disinfection byproducts, following the Guidelines for Canadian Drinking Water Quality in general terms.
tasks.configuration: Scope: baseline byproduct data through the adopted seasonal enhanced dose program.

cards.label: Collect a season of raw and treated total organic carbon, colour, and byproduct results to set the removal goal
Run jar test matrices varying dose and pH together to find the best organics removal with stable alkalinity
Check sludge production and filter run impacts at the candidate doses in a plant scale trial
Select the dose and pH band that meets the organics goal without shortening filter runs below the program limit
Run the selected program for a full production month and sample byproducts at the program points
Adopt the seasonal dose table and set byproduct trending and review dates in the quality program

tasks.explanation: Enhanced coagulation is optimized on organics and byproducts, not turbidity alone, and the adopted dose is proven at plant scale for a month before it becomes the seasonal standard.

tasks.prompt: Order a filter performance optimization program across all plant filters.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Class 3 plant in British Columbia with six dual media filters showing uneven run lengths.
tasks.configuration: Scope: filter data baseline through optimized runs sustained across the filter fleet.

cards.label: Gather run length, headloss, effluent turbidity, and backwash volume data for every filter for one month
Rank filters by performance and inspect the worst filter media depth, surface condition, and underdrain evidence first
Standardize filtration rate and backwash sequence so filters can be compared on equal terms
Trial rate and backwash adjustments on one filter and hold them for three full runs
Extend proven settings to the remaining filters one at a time with the same three run check
Set fleet run length and effluent targets and trend them weekly in the optimization program

tasks.explanation: Fleet optimization standardizes first so comparisons are fair, proves changes on one filter over repeated runs, and only then extends them filter by filter.

tasks.prompt: Order a chemical optimization study covering coagulant, alkali, and disinfectant together.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional regional plant in Alberta seeking lower chemical cost without losing treated quality under provincial requirements in general terms.
tasks.configuration: Scope: chemical use baseline through the adopted optimized chemical program.

cards.label: Total chemical use per treated volume for coagulant, alkali, and chlorine over a representative quarter
Identify the largest use items and the quality result each one protects
Run bench and jar studies to find lower dose combinations that still meet every quality target
Trial the leading combination at plant scale in held steps with quality checks each detention cycle
Confirm residuals handling and filter performance can sustain the new combination
Adopt the optimized doses, update dose tables, and trend chemical use per volume monthly

tasks.explanation: Chemicals are optimized as a system because doses interact, so the study proves a combination at plant scale before any single dose table is changed.

tasks.prompt: Order a plant mass and chemical balance study to locate unexplained chemical loss.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional senior operator in Saskatchewan investigating coagulant use that exceeds the dose record.
tasks.configuration: Scope: balance boundary definition through the loss source corrected and verified.

cards.label: Define the balance boundary from bulk delivery through day tanks, feed pumps, and the application point
Reconcile deliveries, tank level changes, and recorded feed volumes over a closed balance period
Calibrate each feed pump by drawdown and correct the delivered dose record
Compare delivered chemical mass with the mass implied by treated flow and dose
Isolate the gap to one segment by tank and pump checks and correct the leak, overflow, or record error found
Repeat the balance for a second period and close the study only when delivered and applied masses agree

tasks.explanation: A mass balance reconciles what was delivered, what was stored, and what was applied in that order, so a loss is located to one segment before it is corrected.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a sustained settled turbidity creep at steady raw quality.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional conventional plant in western Canada where settled turbidity rose slowly over a week at steady raw quality.
tasks.configuration: Scope: confirmed creep through root cause corrected and settled quality restored.

cards.label: Confirm the creep on the trend record and rule out an instrument drift with a bench settled sample
Check coagulant delivery by drawdown and compare delivered dose with the recorded dose
Inspect rapid mix and flocculation energy, sludge blanket depth, and clarifier flow distribution
Correct the first proven defect and hold all other settings unchanged
Watch settled turbidity for two full detention times to confirm the correction worked
Record the cause, the correction, and a new trend alarm limit in the process log

tasks.explanation: At steady raw quality a creep is an equipment or delivery problem, so delivery and clarifier checks come before any dose increase is considered.

tasks.prompt: Order a disinfection strategy review for a plant with both chlorine and ultraviolet barriers.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Class 3 plant in Manitoba using ultraviolet disinfection followed by free chlorine, under provincial drinking water requirements in general terms.
tasks.configuration: Scope: barrier credit review through the revised disinfection strategy in service.

cards.label: List the inactivation credit assigned to each barrier and the conditions each credit depends on
Review ultraviolet dose, ultraviolet transmittance, and lamp status trends for the review period
Review chlorine residual, temperature, pH, and contact time records for the same period
Identify the weakest combined condition, such as low transmittance with cold water and peak flow
Adjust operating set points so the combined barriers meet the target at the weakest condition
File the revised strategy and brief all shifts on the new set points and alarm responses

tasks.explanation: The strategy is judged at the weakest combined condition, not on average days, so set points are fixed where the two barriers are stressed together.

tasks.prompt: Order a clearwell contact time management program for peak demand season.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in Alberta facing summer peak flows that shorten clearwell contact time.
tasks.configuration: Scope: seasonal demand forecast through peak season contact time protected.

cards.label: Forecast peak day and peak hour flows from the previous three summers and the growth allowance
Calculate contact time at forecast peak flow for each usable clearwell level
Set a minimum peak season clearwell level that still delivers the required contact time
Coordinate storage and distribution pumping so the minimum level is held during peak hours
Verify calculated contact time daily through the peak season and log level, flow, and residual together
Review the season records and revise the level rule before the next peak season

tasks.explanation: Peak season contact time is protected by a level rule set from forecast flows, and daily verification pairs level, flow, and residual so a shortfall is seen the same day.

tasks.prompt: Order a process optimization trial for tube settler clarifiers in cold water.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in northern Saskatchewan with tube settler clarifiers that lose performance in very cold water.
tasks.configuration: Scope: winter baseline through adopted winter clarifier settings.

cards.label: Record winter settled turbidity, blanket behaviour, and sludge withdrawal at current loading rates
Reduce clarifier loading in steps by balancing flow across units and bringing the standby unit into service
Adjust sludge withdrawal frequency to hold the blanket below the tube inlets at the lower loading
Hold each loading step for a full day and compare settled quality at the same raw condition
Select the winter loading and withdrawal settings that hold settled targets with margin
Record the winter settings in the seasonal program and set the spring return criteria

tasks.explanation: Cold water settles more slowly, so winter settings buy settling time through loading and blanket control first, and each step is judged at matched raw conditions.

tasks.prompt: Order a long term treated water quality trend review for utility leadership.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional senior operator in British Columbia presenting five years of treated quality to utility leadership.
tasks.configuration: Scope: data assembled through leadership decisions recorded.

cards.label: Assemble five years of key quality results, incidents, complaints, and process changes on common charts
Separate true trends from changes caused by methods, instruments, or sampling point moves
Identify the three most important trends and the process or source driver behind each
Link each trend to an operational or capital action already planned or newly proposed
Present the trends, drivers, and actions and record the decisions leadership makes
File the review and set the measures that will show whether the actions worked

tasks.explanation: Long term trends are cleaned of method changes before drivers are claimed, and every major trend leaves the room tied to an action and a measure.

tasks.prompt: Order the commissioning of a new online turbidity and particle monitoring program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Class 3 plant in British Columbia adding online instruments on settled and filtered water.
tasks.configuration: Scope: instrument siting through trusted online data used for control.

cards.label: Select sample points that represent settled and each filter effluent without dead legs or air entrainment
Install instruments and verify sample flow, bubble removal, and drain arrangements at each point
Compare online readings with bench results on paired samples across the normal quality range
Set alarm limits from the paired data and the plant quality targets, not from factory defaults
Run the instruments in parallel with bench sampling for two weeks and investigate every major gap
Accept the program for control use and file calibration and comparison records

tasks.explanation: Online data earns control use only after paired bench comparisons across the range and a parallel run that explains every major disagreement.

tasks.prompt: Order a supervisory control and data acquisition alarm rationalization program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional regional plant in western Canada where operators face hundreds of low value alarms each week.
tasks.configuration: Scope: alarm inventory through a rationalized alarm set in service.

cards.label: Export the alarm history for three months and count alarms by point, frequency, and operator response
Classify each alarm as safety, quality critical, equipment protection, or informational
Remove or reclassify alarms that need no operator action and correct chattering alarms at the source
Set deadbands and delays on quality alarms so one excursion raises one alarm
Trial the rationalized set for one month and track alarm rate and missed event reports
Adopt the final alarm list, document the response for each class, and review it quarterly

tasks.explanation: Rationalization keeps alarms that demand action, fixes chattering at the source, and proves the smaller set still catches real events over a trial month.

tasks.prompt: Order a plant energy optimization study for treated water pumping and aeration loads.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in Manitoba ranking its energy use to cut cost per treated volume.
tasks.configuration: Scope: energy baseline through verified savings adopted in the operating program.

cards.label: Meter or estimate energy by major load for a representative month and calculate energy per treated volume
Rank loads and identify off peak shifting, sequencing, and set point opportunities that do not risk quality
Trial the largest opportunity first, such as revised pump sequencing, for two weeks with quality checks
Compare energy per volume and quality results with the baseline at matched flows
Extend proven measures to other loads one at a time with the same comparison
Adopt the measures in the operating program and trend energy per volume monthly

tasks.explanation: Energy measures are proven one at a time at matched flows, so savings are real and any quality effect is tied to the measure that caused it.

tasks.prompt: Order a jar test program upgrade to a full coagulation control laboratory routine.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional senior operator in Alberta upgrading weekly jar tests into a daily control laboratory routine.
tasks.configuration: Scope: routine design through the daily routine adopted by all shifts.

cards.label: Define the daily bench panel: raw and settled turbidity, pH, alkalinity, colour, and treated organics indicator
Standardize jar apparatus, mixing times, and settling times so results compare day to day and shift to shift
Train and check each operator on the bench panel against duplicate samples
Run the routine in parallel with the weekly program for one month and compare dose decisions
Resolve method differences and set control bands for each bench result
Adopt the daily routine, file the method sheets, and schedule monthly duplicate quality checks

tasks.explanation: A control routine is standardized and proven in parallel first, so dose decisions from different shifts rest on the same bench method.

tasks.prompt: Order the seasonal turnover plan for a stratified prairie reservoir source.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in Saskatchewan on a prairie reservoir that turns over in spring and fall with turbidity, manganese, and algae shifts.
tasks.configuration: Scope: turnover forecast through stable treatment after turnover.

cards.label: Track reservoir temperature profile, dissolved oxygen, manganese, and algae counts weekly as turnover approaches
Increase raw sampling frequency and pre run jar tests at the expected turnover quality range
Stage coagulant, alkali, and oxidant inventories for the higher demand period
At turnover, shift to the turnover dose table and shorten settled quality check intervals
Watch filtered manganese and taste and odour results daily until raw quality stabilizes
Return to the normal dose table in steps and file a turnover review with dates and peak raw values

tasks.explanation: Turnover is planned from profile data before it arrives, treatment shifts on a prepared dose table, and the return to normal follows stabilized raw quality.

tasks.prompt: Order the start up of a low pressure membrane plant after a planned shutdown.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional ultrafiltration plant in British Columbia restarting after a two day planned shutdown.
tasks.configuration: Scope: membranes preserved in place through treated water returned to the clearwell.

cards.label: Confirm preservative or wet storage conditions held and inspect trains, valves, and chemical systems
Flush each train to waste at low flow until flush water turbidity and conductivity stabilize
Run an integrity check on each train and hold any train that fails out of service
Start filtration at reduced flux and confirm permeate turbidity on every train
Raise flux in steps to the normal set point while watching transmembrane pressure on each train
Send permeate to the clearwell only after quality is stable and record start up results by train

tasks.explanation: Membrane start up flushes and proves integrity train by train before flux is raised, so no train reaches the clearwell on unverified quality.

tasks.prompt: Order a membrane flux optimization study across a full season.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Class 3 membrane plant in Alberta seeking the highest sustainable flux for its surface water source.
tasks.configuration: Scope: baseline flux performance through the adopted seasonal flux table.

cards.label: Record flux, transmembrane pressure rise, temperature, and cleaning recovery at the current flux for one month
Correct transmembrane pressure trends for temperature so fouling is separated from viscosity effects
Raise flux on one train in small steps, holding each step for at least one week
Watch pressure rise rate and cleaning recovery at each step and stop when recovery falls below the program limit
Set the seasonal flux at the highest step with full cleaning recovery and repeat the check in the cold season
File the flux table by season and set pressure rise alarm limits for each train

tasks.explanation: Sustainable flux is set by cleaning recovery, not by short term pressure alone, and cold water gets its own flux limit because viscosity changes the result.

tasks.prompt: Order the chemically enhanced backwash program for an ultrafiltration train.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional membrane plant in Manitoba using chemically enhanced backwashes to control organic fouling.
tasks.configuration: Scope: fouling diagnosis through the enhanced backwash program in routine service.

cards.label: Confirm from pressure trends and a membrane autopsy or fibre sample that fouling is mainly organic
Select the cleaning chemical and concentration from the membrane supplier program for organic fouling
Set backwash frequency, soak time, and rinse volume and program the sequence on one train
Run the enhanced program on that train for two weeks and compare pressure recovery with a standard train
Check permeate quality and chemical residuals after each enhanced backwash during the trial
Adopt the program for all trains, record chemical use per backwash, and trend recovery weekly

tasks.explanation: The enhanced backwash is matched to the fouling type first, proven on one train against a standard train, and adopted only with permeate quality checks included.

tasks.prompt: Order a clean in place recovery cleaning for a fouled membrane train.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional ultrafiltration train in Saskatchewan whose transmembrane pressure no longer recovers with routine backwashes.
tasks.configuration: Scope: train isolated through cleaning effectiveness verified and train returned.

cards.label: Take the train out of service and record pre cleaning flux, pressure, and integrity status
Prepare the cleaning solution at the supplier specified chemical strength, temperature, and pH
Circulate and soak the train for the full program contact time, keeping temperature in range
Flush the train until rinse water pH and conductivity return to normal feed values
Measure post cleaning flux and pressure at the reference condition and run an integrity check
Return the train only if pressure recovery meets the program target and record chemicals, times, and recovery

tasks.explanation: Recovery cleaning is judged by pressure recovery at a reference condition plus an integrity check, and the train stays out until both pass.

tasks.prompt: Order a membrane integrity testing program using pressure based testing.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional membrane plant in western Canada setting up routine direct integrity testing under provincial drinking water requirements in general terms.
tasks.configuration: Scope: program design through routine integrity results trended by train.

cards.label: Set the test pressure, hold time, and maximum allowable pressure decay for each train from the supplier program
Verify test instruments and isolate the first train with permeate and feed sides in the test configuration
Pressurize, stabilize, and hold the train and record the pressure decay over the full hold time
Compare decay with the allowable limit and investigate any train that exceeds it before further testing
Locate a suspected breach with air based or sonic checks and repair or plug the affected fibres
Retest the repaired train, file results by train, and set the routine test frequency

tasks.explanation: Integrity testing follows a fixed pressure, hold, and decay limit, and a failed train is located, repaired, and retested before it can be trusted again.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a failed membrane integrity test on one train.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional membrane plant in Alberta where one of four trains failed its scheduled integrity test.
tasks.configuration: Scope: failed result confirmed through the repaired train returned to service.

cards.label: Keep the failed train isolated and confirm plant output can be met by the remaining trains
Repeat the test once after checking test connections, valves, and instrument zero to rule out a test error
Inspect with air hold and sonic or visual methods to locate the leaking module or fibre bundle
Repair, plug fibres, or replace the module as the supplier program directs for the defect found
Retest the train at the full test standard and run a permeate turbidity check at start up flux
Return the train, record the defect and repair, and shorten its next test interval

tasks.explanation: A failed test is confirmed before repair so test errors are excluded, and the train returns only on a full passing retest, not on the repair alone.

tasks.prompt: Order a reverse osmosis train performance normalization review.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional reverse osmosis plant in British Columbia treating brackish groundwater for a growing community.
tasks.configuration: Scope: operating data gathered through normalized trends judged and action set.

cards.label: Collect feed pressure, flows, conductivity, temperature, and recovery for each stage for the review period
Normalize permeate flow and salt passage for temperature, pressure, and recovery using the supplier method
Compare normalized trends with the start of run baseline to separate fouling and scaling from condition changes
Identify the stage with the fastest normalized decline and inspect its feed water and antiscalant records
Decide cleaning, antiscalant adjustment, or continued monitoring from the normalized evidence
File the review and set the next normalization interval and cleaning trigger values

tasks.explanation: Normalization removes the effect of temperature and pressure changes, so cleaning decisions rest on true membrane condition rather than on raw trends that move with the weather.

tasks.prompt: Order a reverse osmosis cleaning for scale controlled fouling.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional reverse osmosis plant in Saskatchewan with rising normalized pressure and salt passage in the last stage.
tasks.configuration: Scope: fouling identified as scale through cleaned train performance verified.

cards.label: Confirm scale from normalized trends, concentrate chemistry, and the stage affected
Select the low pH or scale specific cleaning chemical from the supplier program for the scale type
Isolate the train, displace feed with permeate, and prepare the cleaning solution at program strength and temperature
Circulate stage by stage from first to last, holding pH and temperature in range through each soak
Flush until rinse conductivity and pH stabilize and restart at reduced pressure and recovery
Compare normalized permeate flow and salt passage with pre cleaning values and record the recovery

tasks.explanation: Scale cleaning is staged and judged on normalized recovery, and the restart stays at reduced recovery until performance proves the scale is gone.

tasks.prompt: Order a membrane preservative and layup program for a seasonal plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional seasonal membrane plant in northern Manitoba shutting down for the winter freeze period.
tasks.configuration: Scope: final production run through preserved trains protected for the season.

cards.label: Run a recovery cleaning on every train so membranes are stored clean
Flush preservative solution of the supplier specified type and strength through each train until it fills the permeate side
Confirm preservative strength at the train drain points and top up any train below strength
Isolate trains, protect piping from freezing, and set the building heat and alarm checks for the season
Check preservative strength and train condition monthly through the shutdown
Record layup conditions and set the spring flush and integrity test plan before start up

tasks.explanation: Membranes are stored clean and fully preserved, strength is proven at the drains, and monthly checks keep a small layup problem from becoming a spring failure.

tasks.prompt: Order the cold water membrane operating program for winter flux limits.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional membrane plant in northern Alberta where feed water falls near freezing for months.
tasks.configuration: Scope: winter approach through cold season flux and backwash settings in service.

cards.label: Trend feed temperature and note the flux and pressure changes as viscosity rises in the fall
Set the winter flux limit from the supplier cold water guidance and the plant pressure ceiling
Increase backwash frequency if pressure rise accelerates at the winter flux
Confirm permeate quality and integrity test results at the winter settings for the first two weeks
Hold chemical cleaning solutions at program temperature during winter cleanings
Record winter settings and the temperature triggers for entering and leaving the winter program

tasks.explanation: Cold water raises viscosity and pressure at the same flux, so the winter program lowers flux on a temperature trigger and proves quality at the new settings.

tasks.prompt: Order a membrane train rotation and equalization program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional four train membrane plant in western Canada where one train has far more run hours than the others.
tasks.configuration: Scope: run hour audit through balanced train use sustained.

cards.label: Total run hours, backwash counts, and cleaning counts for every train from the control records
Set a rotation that leads with the lowest hour train and rests each train in turn
Equalize flux set points so running trains share load evenly at the same recovery target
Check that rotation does not leave all high hour trains due for cleaning at the same time
Review hours monthly and adjust the lead train order to keep the fleet balanced
File the rotation program and link cleaning schedules to run hours rather than calendar alone

tasks.explanation: Balanced rotation spreads wear and staggers cleaning due dates, so the fleet ages together and capacity is never lost to several trains fouling at once.

tasks.prompt: Order a membrane fouling investigation using feed water and autopsy evidence.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional membrane plant in Saskatchewan with rapid pressure rise that routine cleaning no longer controls.
tasks.configuration: Scope: fouling pattern defined through cause corrected and fouling rate restored.

cards.label: Plot pressure rise rate against feed turbidity, organics, iron, and algae events for the fouling period
Take a fibre or module sample for autopsy under the supplier program and record foulant type and location
Check pretreatment performance, coagulant dose, and prefilter condition for the same period
Match the foulant to its source, such as coagulant carryover or an organics surge
Correct the source first, then run a targeted cleaning matched to the foulant
Trend pressure rise for one month and close the investigation only when the rate returns to the normal band

tasks.explanation: The investigation matches foulant evidence to feed and pretreatment records, corrects the source before cleaning, and closes only on a restored fouling rate.

tasks.prompt: Order the pretreatment optimization program ahead of a membrane plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional membrane plant in British Columbia whose feed quality swings with river conditions.
tasks.configuration: Scope: feed quality baseline through pretreatment settings that protect the membranes.

cards.label: Set membrane feed targets for turbidity, organics indicator, iron, and silt density index where used
Trend feed quality against coagulant dose, prefilter performance, and river condition for one season
Run jar and pilot checks to find the coagulant dose that holds feed targets without carryover
Trial the dose at plant scale and watch membrane pressure rise rate as the deciding result
Set feed quality alarms that reduce flux or stop trains before damaging water reaches the membranes
File the pretreatment program and review feed targets after each major river event

tasks.explanation: Pretreatment is judged by membrane fouling rate, not by feed appearance, and protective alarms act before poor feed can reach the trains at full flux.

tasks.prompt: Order a membrane replacement planning study for an aging train fleet.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Class 3 utility in Alberta planning membrane replacement over a five year horizon.
tasks.configuration: Scope: fleet condition assessment through a funded staged replacement plan.

cards.label: Compile age, run hours, cleaning recovery history, and integrity results for every module group
Test representative modules for permeability and strength under the supplier program
Rank module groups by remaining life and by the quality risk if they fail in service
Stage replacements so at least the required number of trains stays in service in every season
Cost each stage from current supplier pricing and place the stages in the capital plan years
Set condition triggers that can advance a stage if decline accelerates and report the plan to utility management

tasks.explanation: Replacement is staged by measured condition and quality risk, with in service capacity protected in every season and triggers that can advance a stage if decline speeds up.

tasks.prompt: Order the backwash waste recovery program for a membrane plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional membrane plant in Manitoba recovering backwash water to raise overall plant recovery.
tasks.configuration: Scope: backwash waste characterization through recovered water returned under quality control.

cards.label: Measure backwash waste volume, turbidity, and solids across a representative week
Set recovered water quality limits and the equalization and settling steps needed to meet them
Trial returning settled supernatant to the plant inlet at a fixed small share of raw flow
Watch raw and membrane feed quality during the trial for any turbidity or organics creep
Confirm disinfection and membrane performance are unchanged at the trial return share
Adopt the recovery share, set waste quality alarms, and account recovered volume in the plant balance

tasks.explanation: Backwash recovery is adopted at a proven return share with feed quality as the judge, so water savings never come at the cost of membrane fouling.

tasks.prompt: Order a new membrane module acceptance and commissioning sequence.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional membrane plant in western Canada receiving replacement modules for one train.
tasks.configuration: Scope: modules delivered through the commissioned train in full service.

cards.label: Inspect delivered modules for shipping damage and confirm model, serial numbers, and preservative condition
Install modules, flush preservative to waste, and check every connection for leaks at low pressure
Run the supplier wetting and conditioning sequence and measure initial permeability at reference conditions
Run a full integrity test and a permeate quality check before the train carries production
Start the train at reduced flux beside the running trains and compare its pressure trend for one week
Accept the train into full service and file baseline permeability and integrity records

tasks.explanation: New modules earn full service from baseline permeability and a passing integrity test, and their first week trend becomes the reference for later fouling judgments.

tasks.prompt: Order the daily membrane performance review routine for the senior operator.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional senior operator in Saskatchewan running a standing daily membrane review.
tasks.configuration: Scope: overnight data through the daily operating decisions logged.

cards.label: Review flux, transmembrane pressure, temperature, and permeate turbidity for every train
Flag any train whose pressure rise rate exceeds the program band for its feed condition
Check backwash counts, chemical use, and any enhanced backwash or cleaning due that day
Decide flux changes, train rotation, or cleaning for the day and note the reason for each decision
Brief the incoming shift on train status and any train held under watch
File the daily review sheet with the weekly fouling trend summary

tasks.explanation: The daily review ties pressure trends to feed condition and cleaning due dates, so flux and cleaning decisions are made once a day on evidence, not reactively alarm by alarm.

tasks.prompt: Order a concentrate and recovery management program for a reverse osmosis plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional reverse osmosis plant in Alberta balancing recovery against scaling risk on a brackish source.
tasks.configuration: Scope: scaling limit assessment through the adopted recovery set point program.

cards.label: Analyse feed chemistry and calculate the limiting scale at candidate recoveries with the supplier program
Confirm antiscalant type and dose for the limiting scale and verify delivery by drawdown
Raise recovery in small held steps, watching normalized pressure and salt passage at each step
Check concentrate chemistry at each step against the calculated limit with a safety margin
Set the operating recovery at the highest step with stable normalized performance
Trend concentrate and normalized results weekly and set the review trigger if feed chemistry changes

tasks.explanation: Recovery is raised only while normalized performance and concentrate chemistry both hold with margin, so the set point respects the true scaling limit of the source.

tasks.prompt: Order the membrane chemical storage and handling program upgrade.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional membrane plant in British Columbia upgrading storage for cleaning acids, alkalis, and preservatives.
tasks.configuration: Scope: chemical inventory review through the upgraded handling program in use.

cards.label: List every cleaning and preservative chemical, its strength, use rate, and current storage condition
Separate incompatible chemicals with dedicated containment sized for the largest container in each group
Label day tanks and transfer lines by chemical and concentration and remove any unlabelled containers
Train operators on transfer, dilution, and spill response for each chemical and check understanding
Trial the new transfer routine on the next cleaning and correct any labelling or access problems found
File the storage plan, inspection checklist, and training records in the safety program

tasks.explanation: Cleaning chemicals are stored by compatibility with containment and clear labelling first, and the program is proven on a real transfer before it is filed as complete.

tasks.prompt: Order a silt density and feed fouling potential monitoring program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional membrane plant in Manitoba adding feed fouling potential checks to its routine.
tasks.configuration: Scope: monitoring design through feed results driving pretreatment action.

cards.label: Select feed sample points after pretreatment and before each membrane stage
Run fouling potential and turbidity checks on the program schedule and pair them with feed bench results
Plot results against river condition, coagulant dose, and membrane pressure rise rate
Set feed action limits that trigger dose review or flux reduction when fouling potential rises
Act on the first exceedance under the program and record whether pressure rise responded
Review the limits seasonally and file the program with the pretreatment records

tasks.explanation: Feed monitoring earns its place when its limits trigger actions that measurably change fouling rate, so the program is reviewed against pressure trends, not filed and forgotten.

tasks.prompt: Order the ultraviolet reactor validation and duty assignment program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Class 3 plant in Alberta using ultraviolet disinfection under provincial drinking water requirements in general terms.
tasks.configuration: Scope: validated operating range review through duty and standby reactors assigned.

cards.label: Collect the validated flow, transmittance, and dose range for each reactor from its validation record
Confirm installed sensors for flow, intensity, and transmittance are calibrated and reading in range
Assign duty and standby reactors so the duty units cover peak flow inside the validated range
Set the dose control set point with the program safety margin above the required dose
Test automatic standby start on a simulated duty fault and record changeover time and dose
File the duty assignment, set points, and changeover test in the ultraviolet program

tasks.explanation: Duty assignment keeps every running reactor inside its validated range at peak flow, and standby changeover is proven by test, not assumed.

tasks.prompt: Order the ultraviolet lamp aging and replacement program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional ultraviolet plant in Saskatchewan tracking lamp output decline across three reactors.
tasks.configuration: Scope: lamp hour and intensity audit through replaced lamps verified in service.

cards.label: Total lamp run hours and intensity readings for every lamp bank against its commissioning baseline
Identify banks whose intensity at standard conditions has fallen to the program replacement threshold
Order lamps and sleeves and schedule replacement during a low demand window with standby capacity proven
Replace lamps bank by bank, cleaning sleeves and checking seals as each bank is opened
Measure intensity and dose delivery after replacement at reference flow and transmittance
Record new baselines and reset lamp hour counters and file the program update

tasks.explanation: Lamps are replaced on measured intensity decline, one bank at a time with standby proven, and each bank leaves with a new baseline for the next cycle.

tasks.prompt: Order the ultraviolet transmittance monitoring and dose pacing program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in Manitoba whose source transmittance falls during spring runoff and algae season.
tasks.configuration: Scope: transmittance baseline through dose pacing that holds dose in low transmittance water.

cards.label: Install or verify the online transmittance monitor against bench transmittance on paired samples
Trend transmittance against river condition and treated quality for one runoff season
Set dose pacing so reactor power and flow respond to transmittance before dose falls below target
Confirm pacing at the lowest expected transmittance with a controlled flow test
Set low transmittance alarms that reduce plant flow or start the standby reactor
File the pacing program and review transmittance limits before each runoff season

tasks.explanation: Dose pacing acts on transmittance before dose is lost, and the program is proven at the lowest expected transmittance, not at average water.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to an ultraviolet low dose alarm at peak flow.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional ultraviolet plant in British Columbia receiving a low dose alarm during a peak demand afternoon.
tasks.configuration: Scope: alarm confirmed through dose restored and the event reviewed.

cards.label: Check reactor flow, transmittance, lamp status, and intensity readings to confirm the alarm is real
Start the standby reactor and split flow so each reactor returns inside its validated range
Reduce plant flow if dose is still below target after flow is split
Inspect the alarming reactor for lamp, sleeve fouling, or sensor faults once flow is stable
Correct the fault found and return the reactor to duty at reference conditions
Record flows, transmittance, and dose through the event and review whether set points need revision

tasks.explanation: Flow is split and, if needed, reduced before fault finding, because restoring validated dose comes ahead of diagnosing the reactor that lost it.
